Given the vector diagram in figure 4, $\overrightarrow{PQ}=\mathbf{d}$, $\overrightarrow{RQ}=\mathbf{c}$, $\overrightarrow{TP}=\overrightarrow{PQ}$ and M is the mid-point of $\overrightarrow{PR}$.

Find the vector:

figures.legende: Figure 4: horizontal line T, P, Q with vector d drawn from P to Q (TP equal to PQ); vertical segment from R up to Q with vector c; segment PR with its mid-point M.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Go from $P$ to $R$ through $Q$: $\overrightarrow{PR}=\overrightarrow{PQ}+\overrightarrow{QR}$.

$\overrightarrow{PQ}=\mathbf{d}$ and $\overrightarrow{RQ}=\mathbf{c}$, so $\overrightarrow{QR}=-\mathbf{c}$ (the opposite vector).

$\overrightarrow{PR}=\mathbf{d}+(-\mathbf{c})=\mathbf{d}-\mathbf{c}$.

**Answer: $\overrightarrow{PR}=\mathbf{d}-\mathbf{c}$.**
